worldattribute-terraindiffusionEnabled-d: Generate terrain and climate with the Terrain Diffusion neural model instead of the vanilla landform generator.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionScale-des: How many real-world metres one block represents, horizontally and vertically alike.
worldconfig-terraindiffusionScale-30: 30 m per block (most terrain per step)
worldattribute-terraindiffusionVerticalE: Multiplies terrain height above sea level. At 1x a block is exactly as tall as it is wide.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionSeaLevel-: Where the sea sits. Vanilla puts it 43% of the way up, so a taller world spends much of its extra height underground. At Y 128 the rock and ocean below the sea stay 128 blocks deep (a vanilla 256-block world has 110) and every other block goes to the land above it. Climate, soil, trees and weather keep their height above the sea either way.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionClimate-d: Whether the model drives the climate as well as the terrain. The model predicts real bioclimatic variables which set the world's temperature, rainfall, forests and seasons.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionClimateMo: Seasonal also predicts the shape of each place's year, when its rain falls and its day-night temperature swing, which give Köppen climate classes. Annual is the original model. They draw different landscapes from the same seed.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionCoarsePoo: Packs more landscape into the same distance: the model's large-scale map is drawn as usual and every 2x2 or 4x4 block of it squeezed into one cell, so continents, ranges and valleys come closer together and the relief between them steepens. It stays realistic because the model is never asked for anything it was not trained on; 4x is dramatic.

How each squeezed block becomes one cell. Average keeps it realistic. Extreme keeps the highest ground and the deepest valley floor of each block, for taller peaks and deeper cuts, at some cost to realism. Does nothing with terrain intensity off.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionDetailRed: How much of the detail model's first draw is thrown away and redrawn. 0.35 is the model author's quality optimum; higher varies coast shapes and small valleys more.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionHeightNoi: Random height added to the large-scale map (about 8 km of real terrain per cell) before the detail is drawn, for more hills and hollows. 2 is about 100 m at 600 m elevation, more on mountains, none at the coast. 0 is off.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionAltitudeC: How fast it gets colder going up. 100% is the model's own climate; every 100% above that takes another 6.5 C off per kilometre of height, at the ground and in the air alike, so mountains get colder with lower treelines and snowlines. Sea level is unchanged.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionForestDen: Scales the forest cover the model's climate implies. Trees on the ground go roughly as the square of this: 140% is about twice the trees.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionShrubDens: Scales shrub cover the same way, with the same squaring.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionWinterAmp: How much deeper winters get away from the equator: below the annual mean, temperatures swing further by this share at the poles, half of it halfway there. 80% matches vanilla's coldest months. Summers are unchanged; can be changed at any time.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionBandedRai: Asks the model for a third less rain along the latitude bands, a correction measured on the original latitude profile. Off for new worlds.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionRiverVall: How far the land is lowered where the Rivers mod runs a river, so the model shapes a valley to carry it. Needs that mod. High values sink river corridors below sea level and turn them into inlets.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionWaterFill: Fills every closed basin above sea level with fresh water up to where it would spill over, so the model's depressions become lakes and ponds. Off leaves them dry.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionWaterRegi: Lakes are worked out in squares of this many blocks and cannot cross a square's edge. Larger squares allow larger lakes, but a chunk may wait for more of the terrain around it to be generated first.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionInference: Which execution provider runs the model. OpenVINO is primarily for Linux servers. TensorRT RTX needs a GeForce RTX 30xx or newer on Windows or Linux and is roughly 1.5x faster than CUDA. CUDA is another option for Nvidia GPUs. ROCm runs AMD GPUs on Linux and needs ROCm 7 with MIGraphX installed; the first run compiles each model for the GPU, which can take several minutes. "auto" picks CoreML on macOS, DirectML on Windows, CUDA on Linux with an NVIDIA GPU and the CUDA toolkit installed, and the CPU everywhere else. Changing provider can alter newly generated terrain slightly. Takes effect the next time the world is loaded.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionDecoderPr: FP32 is the default. FP16 provides better performance, but kinda sucks atm. INT8 is a smaller decoder for the CPU and OpenVINO. Neither is ever selected automatically because both can alter newly generated terrain slightly. FP16 needs a GPU provider, a world set to it on a machine without one does not load.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionBasePreci: The base model is most of the work in a tile. FP16 with TensorRT-RTX is the fastest, but the default is FP32 until the FP16 model can be improved. FP16 needs a GPU provider, a world set to it on a machine without one does not load.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionGpuUtiliz: Share of the time world generation may keep the inference device busy. Tweaking this may help with stuttering, but can also cause stuttering. Can be changed with /tdiff gpulimit in game.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionCpuThread: How many CPU threads run the model when it runs on the CPU (CPU only, OpenVINO, or a GPU that could not start). Auto is one per physical core, or every thread for OpenVINO. Fewer leaves more for the game. Does not change the terrain. Takes effect the next time the world is loaded.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionOffloadMo: Keep only one of the three models on the GPU at a time. Holds peak VRAM near 1.5 GB instead of about 2.5 GB, and roughly triples the time per terrain tile. Turn on only if the models will not fit on the card. Takes effect the next time the world is loaded.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionModelLoad: Open model graphs directly from their files, or read them into memory first, which costs roughly 1 GB of temporary RAM. Only use from memory if you are also forced to offload models.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionValidateM: Check the SHA-256 of model files already on disk at every start. Turning this off saves a few seconds per start; file sizes are still checked. Takes effect the next time the world is loaded.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionDownloadR: Fetch the matching ONNX Runtime and, when selected, OpenVINO native libraries automatically. Turn off to supply them yourself in TerrainDiffusionModels/onnxruntime/. Takes effect the next time the world is loaded.
worldattribute-terraindiffusionTileDatab: Saves generated terrain to disk so it's never generated twice. Pregenerate with /tdiff pregen. Cleared automatically when the world's terrain settings change. Applies on the next world load.
